source_text: Ὡς γὰρ ἄλλο τὸ πῦρ, καὶ ἄλλο ὁ λύχνος· τὸ μὲν τὴν τοῦ φωτίζειν δύναμιν ἔχον, τὸ δὲ παραφαίνειν τοῖς δεομένοις πεποιημένον· οὕτω καὶ τῷ καθαρωτάτῳ ἐκείνῳ καὶ εἰλικρινεῖ καὶ ἀΰλῳ φωτὶ ὄχημα νῦν οἱ φωστῆρες κατεσκευάσθησαν. Ὡς γὰρ ὁ ἀπόστολος λέγει τινὰς φωστῆρας ἐν κόσμῳ, ἄλλο δέ ἐστι φῶς τοῦ κόσμου τὸ ἀληθινὸν, οὗ κατὰ μέθεξιν οἱ ἅγιοι φωστῆρες ἐγίνοντο τῶν ψυχῶν, ἃς ἐπαίδευον, τοῦ σκότους αὐτὰς τῆς ἀγνοίας ῥυόμενοι· οὕτω καὶ νῦν τὸν ἥλιον τοῦτον τῷ φανοτάτῳ ἐκείνῳ ἐπισκευάσας φωτὶ ὁ τῶν ὅλων δημιουργὸς περὶ τὸν κόσμον ἀνῆψε. 6.3 Καὶ μηδενὶ ἄπιστον εἶναι δοκείτω τὸ εἰρημένον, ὅτι ἄλλο μέν τι τοῦ φωτὸς ἡ λαμπρότης, ἄλλο δέ τι τὸ ὑποκεί μενον τῷ φωτὶ σῶμα. Πρῶτον μὲν οὖν ἐκ τοῦ τὰ σύνθετα πάντα οὕτω παρ' ἡμῶν διαιρεῖσθαι, εἴς τε τὴν δεκτικὴν οὐσίαν, καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐπισυμβᾶσαν αὐτῇ ποιότητα. Ὡς οὖν ἕτερον μέν τι τῇ φύσει ἡ λευκότης, ἕτερον δέ τι τὸ λελευκασμένον σῶμα, οὕτω καὶ τὰ νῦν εἰρημένα, διάφορα ὄντα τῇ φύσει, ἥνωται τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ κτίσαντος. Καὶ μή μοι λέγε ἀδύνατα εἶναι ταῦτα ἀπ' ἀλλήλων διαιρεῖσθαι. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐγὼ τὴν διαίρεσιν τοῦ φωτὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἡλιακοῦ σώματος ἐμοὶ καὶ σοὶ δυνατὴν εἶναί φημι, ἀλλ' ὅτι ἃ ἡμῖν τῇ ἐπινοίᾳ ἐστὶ χωριστὰ, ταῦτα δύναται καὶ αὐτῇ τῇ ἐνεργείᾳ παρὰ τοῦ ποιητοῦ τῆς φύσεως αὐτῶν διαστῆναι. Ἐπεὶ καὶ σοὶ τὴν καυστικὴν δύναμιν τοῦ πυρὸς ἀπὸ τῆς λαμπρότητος χωρίσαι ἀμήχανον· ὁ δὲ Θεὸς παραδόξῳ θεάματι τὸν ἑαυτοῦ θερά ποντα ἐπιστρέψαι βουλόμενος, πῦρ ἐπέθηκε τῇ βάτῳ ἀπὸ μόνης τῆς λαμπρότητος ἐνεργοῦν, τὴν δὲ τοῦ καίειν δύναμιν σχολάζουσαν ἔχον. Ὡς καὶ ὁ ψαλμῳδὸς μαρτυρεῖ λέ γων, Φωνὴ Κυρίου διακόπτοντος φλόγα πυρός. Ὅθεν καὶ ἐν ταῖς τῶν βεβιωμένων ἡμῖν ἀνταποδόσεσι λόγος τις ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀπορρήτῳ παιδεύει, διαιρεθήσεσθαι τοῦ πυρὸς τὴν φύσιν, καὶ τὸ μὲν φῶς, εἰς ἀπόλαυσιν τοῖς δικαίοις, τὸ δὲ τῆς καύσεως ὀδυνηρὸν, τοῖς κολαζομένοις ἀποταχθήσεσθαι. Ἔπειτα μέντοι καὶ ἐκ τῶν περὶ σελήνην παθῶν, δυνατὸν ἡμᾶς τὴν πίστιν τῶν ζητουμένων εὕρασθαι. Λήγουσα γὰρ, καὶ μειουμένη, οὐχὶ τῷ παντὶ ἑαυτῆς σώματι δαπανᾶται, ἀλλὰ τὸ περικείμενον φῶς ἀποτιθεμένη καὶ προσλαμβάνουσα πάλιν, ἐλαττώσεως ἡμῖν καὶ αὐξήσεως τὰς φαντασίας παρέχεται. Τοῦ δὲ μὴ αὐτὸ τὸ σῶμα αὐτῆς ληγούσης ἀπαναλίσκεσθαι ἐναργὲς μαρτύριον τὰ ὁρώμενα. Ἔξεστι γάρ σοι καὶ ἐν καθαρῷ τῷ ἀέρι καὶ πάσης ἀχλύος ἀπηλλαγμένῳ, ὅταν μάλιστα μηνοειδὴς τυγχάνῃ κατὰ τὸ σχῆμα, ἐπιτηρήσαντι κατιδεῖν τὸ ἀλαμπὲς αὐτῆς καὶ ἀφώτιστον ὑπὸ τηλικαύτης ἁψῖδος περιγραφόμενον, ἡλίκον ἐν ταῖς πανσελήνοις τὴν πᾶσαν αὐτὴν ἐκπληροῖ. Ὥστε τηλαυγῶς ἀπηρτισμένον καθορᾶσθαι τὸν κύκλον τῷ περιλαμπομένῳ μέρει τὸν σκιερὸν καὶ ἀερώδη κόλπον συναναφερούσης τῆς ὄψεως. Καὶ μή μοι λέγε ἐπείσακτον εἶναι τῆς σελήνης τὸ φῶς, διότι μειοῦται μὲν πρὸς ἥλιον φερομένη, αὔξεται δὲ πάλιν ἀφισταμένη. Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐκεῖνο ἡμῖν ἐξετάζειν ἐν τῷ παρόντι πρόκειται, ἀλλ' ὅτι ἕτερον μὲν αὐτῆς τὸ σῶμα, ἕτερον δὲ τὸ φωτίζον.
thought_title: Light and its vehicle are distinct
orientation: Basil is explaining the fourth day of creation, arguing that the sun and moon are not the light itself but vehicles prepared for the first-created light.
pass_a_gloss: For as fire is one thing, and the lamp another—the one having the power of giving light, the other made to shine beside for those in need—so also for that purest and unmixed and immaterial light the lights have now been prepared as a vehicle. For as the apostle says certain lights in the world, but the true light of the world is another thing, by participation in which the holy ones became lights of the souls which they were teaching, rescuing them from the darkness of ignorance; so also now the maker of all things, having fitted this sun to that most radiant light, kindled it around the world. And let what has been said seem unbelievable to no one, that the brightness of the light is one thing, and the body underlying the light is another thing. First, then, from the fact that all composite things are thus divided by us, into the receptive substance and into the quality that has come upon it. As therefore whiteness is one thing in nature, and the whitened body another thing, so also the things now said, being different in nature, have been united by the power of the creator. And do not tell me that these things are impossible to be divided from one another. For neither do I say that the division of the light from the solar body is possible for me and you, but that the things which are separable for us in thought, these things can also in actual operation be separated by the maker of their nature. Since also for you to separate the burning power of fire from the brightness is impossible; but God, wishing to turn his servant by a paradoxical spectacle, placed fire on the bush, active from the brightness alone, and having the power of burning idle. As also the psalmist testifies, saying, The voice of the Lord who divides the flame of fire. Whence also in the recompenses of the things lived by us a certain teaching instructs us in secret, that the nature of fire will be divided, and the light for enjoyment to the righteous, but the painful part of burning will be assigned to those being punished. Then indeed also from the experiences concerning the moon, it is possible for us to find the faith of the things being sought. For waning and decreasing, it is not consumed in its whole body, but putting off and taking on again the surrounding light, it provides to us the appearances of decrease and increase. And that the body itself of the waning moon is not consumed, the things seen are a clear testimony. For it is possible for you, in clear air and air freed from all mist, when especially it happens to be crescent-shaped in form, having observed, to see its unlit and unilluminated part circumscribed by such an arc, as great as in full moons fills the whole of it. So that the completed circle is clearly seen, the sight bringing up together with the illuminated part the shadowy and airy hollow. And do not tell me that the light of the moon is imported, because it decreases when moving toward the sun, and increases again when withdrawing. For neither is that proposed for us to examine at present, but that its body is one thing, and the thing giving light is another.

choices.why: Basil uses the image of a vehicle to express that the sun and moon carry the pre-existing light; 'vehicle' preserves the metaphor of transport rather than a container.

choices.term: τῷ καθαρωτάτῳ ἐκείνῳ καὶ εἰλικρινεῖ καὶ ἀΰλῳ φωτὶ
choices.english: that purest and unmixed and immaterial light
choices.why: The three adjectives distinguish the first-created light from physical light; 'unmixed' renders εἰλικρινεῖ as free from admixture, and 'immaterial' renders ἀΰλῳ as without matter.
rejected: that most pure and sincere and bodiless light
that purest, clearest, and immaterial light

choices.why: The verb means to equip or prepare something for use; 'fitted' conveys the sense of adapting the sun to serve the light, matching the earlier 'vehicle' image.
The verb means to light or kindle a fire; Basil uses it to describe God setting the sun alight with the pre-existing light, preserving the fire/lamp imagery.
The term means brought in from outside; 'imported' captures the idea that the moon's light is not its own but comes from elsewhere, which Basil is setting aside as not the present question.
The participle means brought to completion or made whole; Basil says the full circle of the moon is seen as complete, so 'completed' renders the perfect passive sense.

pass_b_english: For just as fire is one thing and a lamp another—the one possessing the power to give light, the other made to shine for those who need it—so also the lights were now prepared as a vehicle for that purest and unmixed and immaterial light. For as the apostle says, there are certain lights in the world (Philippians 2:15), but the true light of the world is something else (John 1:9), and by sharing in it the saints became lights for the souls they taught, rescuing them from the darkness of ignorance. In the same way, the Maker of all things fitted this sun to that most radiant light and kindled it around the world.

And let no one think what has been said is unbelievable—that the brightness of light is one thing, and the body underlying the light is another. First, then, from the fact that all composite things are divided by us in this way, into the receptive substance and the quality that has come upon it. Just as whiteness is one thing by nature and the whitened body another, so also the things now spoken of, being different by nature, have been united by the power of the Creator. And do not tell me that it is impossible for these to be divided from one another. For I do not claim that the division of light from the solar body is possible for you and me, but that what is separable for us in thought can also be separated in actual operation by the Maker of their nature. Since even for you it is impossible to separate the burning power of fire from its brightness; yet God, wishing to turn his servant by a marvelous sight, placed fire on the bush that was active from its brightness alone, while its power to burn remained idle (Exodus 3:2). As the psalmist also testifies when he says, “The voice of the Lord divides the flame of fire” (Psalm 28:7 LXX). From this also, in the repayment of the lives we have lived, a certain teaching instructs us in mystery: that the nature of fire will be divided, and the light will be assigned for the enjoyment of the righteous, while the painful part of burning will be appointed for those being punished.

Then, moreover, from the phenomena concerning the moon, it is possible for us to find faith in what we are seeking. For when it wanes and decreases, it is not consumed in its whole body, but by putting off the light that surrounds it and taking it on again, it presents to us the appearances of decrease and increase. And that its body itself is not consumed when it wanes has clear testimony in what is seen. For you can, in clear air free from all mist, especially when it happens to be crescent-shaped, observe and see its unlit and unilluminated part outlined by an arc as large as the one that fills the whole of it at full moon. So the completed circle is clearly seen, with the eye bringing together the shadowy and misty hollow with the illuminated part. And do not tell me that the moon's light is imported, because it decreases as it moves toward the sun and increases again as it draws away. For that is not what we are examining at present, but rather that its body is one thing, and what gives it light is another.

last_rejected.why: "εὕρασθαι" is aorist middle infinitive, "to obtain/find for oneself"—"find faith" is slightly odd; "obtain conviction" or "find confirmation" would be closer. The English is somewhat misleading, suggesting "finding religious faith" rather than "finding confirmation/conviction for what we seek."

last_rejected.ruling: πίστιν here means 'conviction/assurance'; 'find faith' is within acceptable range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: The English adds parenthetical scripture references not in the source. The brief says to check if "a cited Bible reference does not match the words quoted or alluded to." Philippians 2:15 has "φωστῆρες ἐν κόσμῳ" (lights in the world), and John 1:9 has "τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν" (the true light). These are correct identifications of Basil's allusions. However, the source does not explicitly cite these references—Basil says "as the apostle says" without naming Paul or giving a book. The English adds specificity. Is this an "addition"? The brief says "English states something the source does not"—the source does not state Philippians 2:15 or John 1:9. However, the brief's "wrong_scripture" category is about "a cited Bible reference does not match the words quoted or alluded to"—these do match. The addition of references is translatorial choice, not a meaning error. Not reportable per instructions (glossary and name choices checked elsewhere; don't report style preferences).
last_rejected.ruling: Added parenthetical refs correctly identify allusions; Phil 2:15 and John 1:9 match source words. Not a meaning error.
